questions.q: What is the IUPAC name of (CH₃)₃C–Br?
questions.explain: The parent chain is propane with both –Br and –CH₃ on C-2; so 2-bromo-2-methylpropane (tertiary).

questions.q: Which of the following is a vinylic halide?
questions.explain: In a vinylic halide the halogen is on an sp² carbon of C=C. CH₂=CHCH₂Cl is allylic and C₆H₅CH₂Cl is benzylic.

questions.q: What is the advantage of using SOCl₂ to prepare an alkyl chloride from an alcohol?
options: The by-products SO₂ and HCl are gases, so the product is pure
questions.explain: SO₂ and HCl escape as gases, so a pure alkyl chloride is obtained.

questions.q: What is the name of the reaction in which an alkyl chloride reacts with NaI in dry acetone to give an alkyl iodide?
questions.explain: NaCl is insoluble in acetone and precipitates, so the reaction goes forward. The Swarts reaction gives fluorides.

questions.q: Which of the following has the highest boiling point?
questions.explain: For the same group RI > RBr > RCl > RF, because van der Waals forces grow with size.

questions.q: What is the order of reactivity of alkyl halides in SN2?
questions.explain: The less the steric hindrance the faster the SN2; the tertiary halide has the most hindrance.

questions.q: What is the rate law of an SN2 reaction?
questions.explain: SN2 is second order — the rate depends on the concentrations of both the halide and the nucleophile.

questions.q: What is the rate determining step in an SN1 reaction?
questions.explain: The first step, in which the C–X bond breaks and the carbocation forms, is slow, so it determines the rate.

questions.q: What does optically active (+)-2-bromooctane give with OH⁻ in an SN2 reaction?
questions.explain: In SN2 back-side attack inverts the configuration — the (+)-bromide gives the (−)-alcohol.

questions.q: Which of the following compounds is chiral?
questions.explain: C-2 of butan-2-ol carries four different groups: –H, –OH, –CH₃ and –C₂H₅.

questions.q: Why is a racemic mixture optically inactive?
options: It contains equal amounts of two enantiomers whose rotations cancel
questions.explain: Rotations of equal magnitude and opposite direction make the total rotation zero.

questions.q: What is the major product when 2-bromopentane is heated with alcoholic KOH?
questions.explain: By Zaitsev's rule the more substituted alkene (pent-2-ene, 81 %) is the major product.

questions.q: Why is a Grignard reagent kept away from water?
options: It reacts with water to give a hydrocarbon
questions.explain: RMgX + H₂O → RH + Mg(OH)X; the reagent is destroyed.

questions.q: Why is chlorobenzene less reactive in nucleophilic substitution?
options: Because of resonance the C–Cl bond has partial double bond character
questions.explain: The lone pair of the halogen conjugates with the ring and strengthens the C–Cl bond.

questions.q: Which of the following is the most reactive in nucleophilic substitution?
questions.explain: The more –NO₂ groups at ortho and para positions, the easier the reaction; the trinitro compound reacts even with warm water.

questions.q: What is the main environmental problem with the use of Freon-12 (CCl₂F₂)?
questions.explain: In the stratosphere it produces free radicals that destroy ozone.
